question: Should memory-lancedb autoCapture reject OpenClaw-authored EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrappers by default, or should this be exposed as a new captureFilter configuration option?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent fix defines a security boundary and possibly a new public config surface, so automation should not choose the policy.

options.title: Reject wrappers by default
options.body: Treat OpenClaw external-content wrappers as a host-owned capture boundary before shouldCapture and add regression coverage across wrapped external inputs.

options.title: Add captureFilter config
options.body: Introduce a documented operator-controlled excludeWrapped option with schema, manifest, docs, and upgrade-safe default tests.

options.title: Defer to provenance architecture
options.body: Leave this narrow filter open until broader memory trust/provenance work defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject wrappers by default
recommendation.body: Treat OpenClaw external-content wrappers as a host-owned capture boundary before shouldCapture and add regression coverage across wrapped external inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice crosses external-content security wrappers and persistent memory behavior, and vincentkoc has recent history in the wrapper sanitization path.
